claims: As of April 2026, the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) is temporarily suspending employer contributions to the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS).
The suspension aims to save approximately $2.5 billion through September 30.
The suspension is by pausing $200 million in biweekly payments.
Officials state there is no immediate impact on current or future retirees.
USPS is halting its employer contributions to the FERS defined benefit plan.
USPS will continue to transmit employee contributions to FERS.
USPS will continue contributions to the Thrift Savings Plan (TSP).
USPS will continue contributions to Social Security.
USPS reported $118 billion in net losses since 2007.
USPS quarterly losses reached $1.25 billion in early 2026.
The Postal Service previously suspended these payments in 2011 during a similar financial crisis.
Career employees are covered under FERS or the Civil Service Retirement System (CSRS).
USPS must fund its retirement obligations through its own operating revenue.
All three retirement-related funds (including health benefits) have unfunded liabilities.
